question.value: Examine the constraints on dust physics and obscured star formation in the z > 8 Universe by stacking deep (sub)mm observations of ten spectroscopically confirmed galaxies.

evidence.quote: In this study, we examine the constraints on dust physics provided by existing deep ($t_{\rm int} > 1$ hr) (sub)mm observations of galaxies with robust redshifts in the $z > 8$ Universe.

evidence.loc: The present and future of dust studies in the $z > 8$ Universe
evidence.quote: One exciting opportunity for stacking studies is the COSMOS High-$z$ ALMA-MIRI Population Survey (CHAMPS) ALMA Large Program (PID: 2023.1.00180.L; P.I. A. Faisst).
ALMA observations targeted the expected region where the \[O iii\] 88 $\mu{\rm m}$ emission was located in project 2019.1.00397.S (P.I. Takuya Hashimoto; Arai et al. in prep.)
Deep ALMA observations (2019.1.00397.S; P.I. Takuya Hashimoto and 2022.1.01562.S; P.I. Seiji Fujimoto; Arai et al. in prep.) provide deep upper limits but no confirmation of the high redshift.

Even though both fields enjoy deep ALMA observations in an effort to confirm their high-redshift nature through the \[O iii\] 88 $\mu{\rm m}$ and dust emission (2022.1.01562.S; P.I. S. Fujimoto and 2021.1.00389.S; Takuya Hashimoto; Arai et al. in prep.)
Subsequent ALMA imaging (2019.A.00015.S; P.I. Akio Inoue) provided a tentative $4 \sigma$ \[O iii\] 88 $\mu{\rm m}$ at the expected redshift
This stacking study is made possible by the continued work on ALMA receivers in Bands 5, 6, 7, and 8 (cite: Belitsky2018; Ediss2004; Mahieu2012; Sekimoto2008).

findings_qualitative.value: No significant (>3 sigma) dust continuum emission is detected in any of the individual z > 8 galaxies (excluding MACS0416-Y1) or in any of the 21 stacked maps across flux, dust mass, dust-to-stellar mass ratio, or sub-bins.

evidence.quote: None of the stacks have led to a $> 3 \sigma$ detection, although the $\beta_{\rm UV} > -2$ (i.e., dustier UV-continuum slope) indicate a $2 \sigma$ feature in the flux and dust-to-stellar mass ratio stack.

findings_qualitative.value: Dust build-up in the z > 8 Universe is inefficient compared to z < 8, requiring a rapid transition in dust formation efficiency or timescale between z > 8 and z < 8, or efficient dust removal via galactic outflows.

evidence.quote: the low estimated dust-to-stellar mass ratios of $\log_{10} M_{\rm dust} / M_{\ast} < -3.5$ to $-3$ support inefficient dust production in the early Universe, and are in line with a rapid transition in dust production efficiencies or timescales between $z > 8$ and $z < 8$.

findings_qualitative.value: UV-derived optical dust mass estimates exceed the sub-mm dust mass upper limits for all stacks and several individual galaxies, showing that simple optical measures of dust mass are unreliable at z > 8.

evidence.quote: Several individually-observed sources and, more importantly all of the stacks find higher optical dust masses than the sub-mm dust mass limits.
that the optical measures of dust masses are unreliable, both for individual sources and for the stacks, in line with previous studies of detected $z < 8$ galaxies (cite: Sommovigo2022).

claims.hypothesis: Deep stacking of ~175 hours of ALMA and NOEMA observations of ten spectroscopically confirmed z > 8 galaxies can detect average dust continuum emission or place stringent limits on early-Universe dust reservoirs.
claims.experiment: Re-calibrated and re-imaged archival ALMA observations (plus NOEMA data for GN-z11) and stacked them in the image plane using LINESTACKER weighted by flux density, dust mass, and dust-to-stellar mass ratio across the full sample and binned by redshift, stellar mass, and UV slope.
claims.result: No emission is detected at >3 sigma in any stack, yielding 1-sigma depths of 2.0, 2.0, and 1.5 uJy at rest-frame 158 um, 88 um, and across all data, corresponding to 3-sigma upper limits of M_dust < 9.1 x 10^4 M_sun (dust-weighted) or 4.6 x 10^5 M_sun (flux-weighted) and M_dust/M_* < 3.7 x 10^-4 for T_dust = 50 K and beta_dust = 2.
claims.finding: Average dust reservoirs in UV-selected z > 8 galaxies are below 10^5 M_sun and no sub-population in redshift, stellar mass, or UV slope shows significant dust emission.

evidence.quote: This study combines around two hundred hours of Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and Northern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA) observations on ten $z > 8$ galaxies, revealing no significant dust emission down to a $1 \sigma$ depth of $2.0$, $2.0$, and $1.5 \,\mu$Jy at rest-frame 158, 88 $\mu$m, and across all the data, respectively.

a deep upper limit on the dust mass, with a typically observed galaxy containing dust reservoir smaller than $9.1 \times{} 10^4$ M$_{\odot}$, assuming a dust temperature of $T_{z = 0} = 50$ K and $\beta_{\rm dust} = 2$.

claims.hypothesis: Dust build-up in galaxies at z > 8 is inefficient compared to galaxies at z < 8.
claims.experiment: Compared the individual and stacked z > 8 dust masses and dust-to-stellar mass ratios against z < 8 detections/stacks (ALPINE, REBELS, cosmic noon) and theoretical dust evolution models and hydrodynamical simulations.
claims.result: The z > 8 dust-to-stellar mass ratios (log10 M_dust/M_* < -3.5 to -3) lie below typical z < 8 values (log10 M_dust/M_* > -3) and below prolific dust production models, matching only models with inefficient grain growth, high destruction, or low halo masses.
claims.finding: Dust production is inefficient at z > 8 (likely due to limited time for AGB stars, inefficient SN production/grain growth, or outflow ejection) and must rapidly transition to higher efficiency at z < 8.

evidence.loc: Dust build-up in the early Universe
evidence.quote: The dust-to-stellar mass ratio measures of individual sources and stacks lie below typically-observed values in the more nearby Universe at $z < 8$ of $\log_{10} M_{\rm dust} / M_{\ast} > -3$, with the only source at $z > 8$ in line with $\log_{10} M_{\rm dust} / M_{\ast} = -3$.

the low estimated dust-to-stellar mass ratios of $\log_{10} M_{\rm dust} / M_{\ast} < -3.5$ to $-3$ support inefficient dust production in the early Universe, and are in line with a rapid transition in dust production efficiencies or timescales between $z > 8$ and $z < 8$.

claims.hypothesis: Rest-frame UV continuum slopes (beta_UV) and optical sizes can reliably predict the total dust mass of z > 8 galaxies via standard attenuation laws.
claims.experiment: Calculated optically-derived dust masses using UV sizes and the Meurer attenuation law (following Ferrara et al. 2022) and compared them against the sub-mm dust mass upper limits for individual galaxies and stacks.
claims.result: All stacked bins and several individual sources have optically-derived dust masses higher than the 3-sigma sub-mm dust mass upper limits (e.g., 57 x 10^4 M_sun optical vs < 9.1 x 10^4 M_sun sub-mm for the full stack).
claims.finding: Optical measures of dust mass are unreliable at z > 8 under standard geometry and attenuation assumptions, pointing to spatial offsets, different dust properties/temperatures, or dusty outflows.

evidence.quote: Several individually-observed sources and, more importantly all of the stacks find higher optical dust masses than the sub-mm dust mass limits.
that the optical measures of dust masses are unreliable, both for individual sources and for the stacks, in line with previous studies of detected $z < 8$ galaxies (cite: Sommovigo2022).

why_this_data.value: Limited to galaxies with robust spectroscopic confirmations at z > 8 and deep (> 1 hr) interferometric observations to prevent contamination from low-redshift interlopers in the stacks.

evidence.quote: To avoid the confusing effect of interlopers in this stacking experiment, this study is limited to all objects that are robustly confirmed to lie at $z > 8$.

why_this_method.value: Image-plane stacking with LINESTACKER allows combining heterogeneous observations from different cycles and facilities (ALMA and NOEMA) with custom physical weightings; flux-weighted dust masses are reported conservatively to avoid domination by single strongly-lensed objects.

evidence.quote: Given the large variation in observations from different observation cycles and necessary weighting schemes, the stacking is performed in the image plane (cite: Lindroos2015). This furthermore facilitates the combination of NOEMA and ALMA data, as well as making the tool readily available for the public.

evidence.loc: Choice of stacking method for reporting results
evidence.quote: The flux-based dust mass estimate is about a factor five times more conservative than the dust-stacked mass estimate, but better samples our full galaxy population, avoiding over-weighting of individual lensed systems while still benefiting from the improved sensitivity of stacking (see e.g., Fig 3).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Smoothing all images to a common beam larger than the largest individual beam before stacking (rejected because it increased per-beam noise by > 3x in high-resolution maps).

evidence.quote: A smoothing to a common beam larger than the largest individual beam was attempted, but resulted in strong ($\sigma_{\rm smoothed} > 3 \times{} \sigma_{\rm unsmoothed}$) increases in the per-beam noise of the sources with the highest-resolution observations.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Including SPT-0615-JD, COS-z-0/COS-z12-1, and unconfirmed z > 8 candidates in the stack (rejected due to extended emission beyond the beam, foreground galaxy confusion, and risk of low-redshift interlopers, respectively).

how_they_decided_enough.value: Restricted sub-sample binning to three physically motivated parameters (redshift, stellar mass, and beta_UV) to avoid false positives from p-hacking.

evidence.loc: Binning by redshift, $\beta$ and stellar mass
evidence.quote: In total, we chose criteria to separate the population of galaxies, namely redshift, stellar mass and UV spectral slope ($\beta_{\rm UV}$). Although more binning options are imaginable, these result in a higher chance of false positives through *p-hacking*, and the scientific motivation behind these three bins appears most robust.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust mass limits assume a fixed dust temperature (T_dust = 50 K at z = 0) and emissivity index (beta_dust = 2); varying T_dust by +/- 10 K changes dust masses by a factor of ~2, varying beta_dust by +/- 0.5 changes them by ~25%, and internal temperature variations could cause up to 0.25 dex underestimation.

evidence.quote: If the assumed dust temperature is changed by $\pm 10$ K, the predicted dust masses across the entire sample changes roughly by a factor of two, with the colder dust temperature predicting higher dust masses and vice versa. If the assumed dust emissivity index $\beta_{\rm dust}$ is changed by $\pm 0.5$, the predicted dust masses across the entire sample changes by roughly 25 per cent

Recent analytical modeling (cite: Sommovigo2025DifferentTdistributions) predicts under-estimation of the dust mass up to 0.25 dex at $T_{z = 0} = 50$ K for realistic internal dust temperature variations $\sigma_{T} / \bar{T} < 0.3$

limitations_admitted.value: Stellar masses are taken from literature using diverse spectral fitting approaches, introducing systematic uncertainties into the dust-to-stellar mass ratios.

evidence.loc: Stacking to a single dust-to-stellar mass ratio
evidence.quote: Here, we note the important caveat that the diversity in spectral fitting approaches can result in systematically different stellar masses across the sample.

limitations_admitted.value: Gravitational lensing is assumed to affect dust and stellar emission equally, ignoring potential differential lensing.

evidence.loc: Stacking to a single dust-to-stellar mass ratio
evidence.quote: The effect of gravitational lensing is presumed to affect the stellar and dust components equally, ignoring any effects of differential lensing (cite: serjeant2012), and is thus effectively negated in the per-pixel measure of the dust-to-stellar mass ratio.

limitations_admitted.value: UV-preselection of the sample biases it toward UV-bright galaxies and may miss heavily dust-obscured (optically-dark) systems at z > 8.

evidence.quote: As seen in Figure 1, many of the galaxies in this survey are the UV-brightest objects. This UV-preselection can result in missing the most dust-obscured systems at a given redshift, as exemplified by so-called optically-dark galaxies seen out to $z > 7$ (cite: Fudamoto2021OpticallyDark).

referee_caveats_inferred: Stacking unsmoothed maps with beam sizes varying from 0.37 to 1.35 arcsec assumes all sources are strictly point-like; any extended dust component (such as dusty outflows discussed in the text) would be partially resolved out in the smaller-beam observations.
Excluding the only sub-mm detected z > 8 galaxy (MACS0416-Y1) from the stacks, while useful to probe the undetected population, biases the sample average downward.
